steps: 1. Put a 1 under the whole number: 3 ÷ 1/4 = 3/1 ÷ 1/4

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Snack Bags
revealWordProblem.text:
Andrew has four types of nuts and a different quantity of each type, shown on the bags. He wants to make 4 snack bags of each type of nut, and he will not mix the nuts together in a bag.
Question: What will be the weight of the snack bags for each type of nut? Explain your reasoning.
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: Four bags of nuts labeled with their weights: almonds one-half pound, cashews one-fourth pound, peanuts two-fifths pound, walnuts three-fourths pound.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Each amount is being shared equally among 4 bags, so divide each weight by 4. Almonds: ½ ÷ 4 = ⅛ pound per bag. Cashews: ¼ ÷ 4 = 1/16 pound per bag. Peanuts: ⅖ ÷ 4 = 1/10 pound per bag. Walnuts: ¾ ÷ 4 = 3/16 pound per bag. Dividing by 4 is the same as multiplying by ¼, which is why every answer is smaller than the amount Andrew started with.

questions.explanation: 3 ÷ 1/4 asks how many 1/4-size pieces fit into 3. To find that, put a 1 under the 3 and use Keep, Change, Flip: 3/1 × 4/1 = 12.
choiceFeedback: That's finding a part of the whole. Division by a fraction asks 'how many of this size fit inside.'
That's multiplication (3 × 1/4). Division asks 'how many' pieces, not 'groups of' pieces.
Subtraction is not division. Division by a fraction asks 'how many pieces fit.'
hints: Re-read the expression: 3 is the total amount and 1/4 is the size of one piece. What question could that setup be asking?
Dividing by a fraction asks a counting question about pieces, not 'a part of.' Predict: should the result be bigger or smaller than 3?
Picture a 3-foot tape cut into 1/4-foot pieces, then set it up: put a 1 under the 3 and flip the 1/4.
questions.explanationEs: 3 ÷ 1/4 pregunta cuántas piezas del tamaño de 1/4 caben en 3. Para hallarlo, pon un 1 debajo del 3 y usa Conserva, Cambia, Voltea: 3/1 × 4/1 = 12.
choicesEs: Cuántas piezas de tamaño 1/4 caben en 3
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer la expresión: 3 es la cantidad total y 1/4 es el tamaño de una pieza. ¿Qué pregunta podría estar haciendo ese planteamiento?
Dividir entre una fracción hace una pregunta de conteo sobre piezas, no de 'una parte de'. Predice: ¿el resultado debe ser mayor o menor que 3?
Imagina una cinta de 3 pies cortada en piezas de 1/4 de pie y luego plantéalo: pon un 1 debajo del 3 y voltea el 1/4.

questions.stem: Which expression means 'how many 1/3-size pieces are in 2'?
questions.explanation: Finding how many 1/3-size pieces fit into 2 is written 2 ÷ 1/3. Put a 1 under the 2, then Keep, Change, Flip: 2/1 × 3/1 = 6.
choiceFeedback: You flipped the order. The whole (2) goes first; the piece size (1/3) is the divisor.
That multiplies instead of divides. To find how many pieces fit, we divide by the piece size.
Addition combines amounts. To find how many pieces fit, we divide.
hints: Find the two jobs: which number is the total being split, and which is the size of each piece?
Division setups read total ÷ piece size. The total always sits in front of the ÷ sign.
Here the total is 2 and each piece is 1/3. Build the expression with the total first, then check it against each choice.
questions.stemEs: ¿Qué expresión significa "cuántas piezas del tamaño de 1/3 hay en 2"?
questions.explanationEs: Encontrar cuántas piezas del tamaño de 1/3 caben en 2 se escribe 2 ÷ 1/3. Pon un 1 debajo del 2 y luego Conserva, Cambia, Voltea: 2/1 × 3/1 = 6.
hintsEs: Encuentra los dos papeles: ¿cuál número es el total que se reparte y cuál es el tamaño de cada pieza?
Los planteamientos de división se leen total ÷ tamaño de la pieza. El total siempre va delante del signo ÷.
Aquí el total es 2 y cada pieza es 1/3. Arma la expresión con el total primero y luego compárala con cada opción.

questions.stem: A rope is 4 feet long. How many 1/2-foot pieces can be cut from it?
questions.explanation: Write 4 ÷ 1/2. Put a 1 under the 4, then Keep, Change, Flip: 4/1 × 2/1 = 8 pieces.
choiceFeedback: You did not flip the divisor. Put a 1 under the 4, flip 1/2 to 2/1, then multiply.
You divided 4 by 2. Dividing by 1/2 means flipping it: 4/1 × 2/1 = 8.
Dividing by 1/2 makes the answer bigger. Flipping 1/2 gives 2/1, a factor larger than 1.
hints: Note the numbers: the rope is 4 feet long, and every piece is 1/2 foot — smaller than a whole foot.
Start small: figure out how many 1/2-foot pieces fit into just 1 foot of rope.
Put a 1 under the 4 to get 4/1, then Keep, Change, Flip: 4/1 × 2/1.
questions.stemEs: Una cuerda mide 4 pies de largo. ¿Cuántas piezas de 1/2 pie se pueden cortar de ella?
questions.explanationEs: Escribe 4 ÷ 1/2. Pon un 1 debajo del 4 y luego Conserva, Cambia, Voltea: 4/1 × 2/1 = 8 piezas.
hintsEs: Fíjate en los números: la cuerda mide 4 pies y cada pieza mide 1/2 pie, menos que un pie entero.
Empieza en pequeño: averigua cuántas piezas de 1/2 pie caben en solo 1 pie de cuerda.
Pon un 1 debajo del 4 para obtener 4/1 y luego Conserva, Cambia, Voltea: 4/1 × 2/1.

questions.stem: The model shows a 3-foot ribbon cut into 1/4-foot pieces. Which expression does the model represent, and how many pieces are there?
choiceFeedback: That multiplies. 3 × 1/4 finds 1/4 OF the ribbon, but the model cuts the ribbon up and counts the pieces.
You divided in the wrong order. The 3-foot ribbon is the amount being cut, so it goes first: 3 ÷ 1/4.
You divided by 4 instead of by 1/4. Dividing by 4 makes 4 long pieces; the model shows small 1/4-foot pieces, and there are more of them than 3.
questions.explanation: Each of the 3 feet holds four 1/4-foot pieces, so the model shows 12 pieces in all. Written as an expression that is 3 ÷ 1/4. Put a 1 under the 3, then Keep, Change, Flip: 3/1 × 4/1 = 12.
hints: Read the model first: how long is the whole ribbon, and how long is each small piece?
The model cuts a whole into equal small pieces and counts them. That is a division question — total ÷ piece size — so the total goes in front of the ÷ sign.
Count the 1/4-foot parts in all three feet, then check it: put a 1 under the 3 and flip the 1/4 to get 3/1 × 4/1.
questions.stemEs: El modelo muestra una cinta de 3 pies cortada en piezas de 1/4 de pie. ¿Qué expresión representa el modelo y cuántas piezas hay?
questions.explanationEs: Cada uno de los 3 pies contiene cuatro piezas de 1/4 de pie, así que el modelo muestra 12 piezas en total. Escrito como expresión es 3 ÷ 1/4. Pon un 1 debajo del 3 y luego Conserva, Cambia, Voltea: 3/1 × 4/1 = 12.
hintsEs: Primero lee el modelo: ¿cuánto mide la cinta entera y cuánto mide cada pieza pequeña?
El modelo corta un entero en piezas iguales y las cuenta. Esa es una pregunta de división — total ÷ tamaño de la pieza — así que el total va delante del signo ÷.
Cuenta las partes de 1/4 de pie en los tres pies y luego compruébalo: pon un 1 debajo del 3 y voltea el 1/4 para obtener 3/1 × 4/1.

steps: 1. Put a 1 under the whole number: 3 ÷ 1/4 = 3/1 ÷ 1/4
reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Interpret Division of Fractions is assuming that dividing always makes the answer smaller. For 4 ÷ 1/3, students reason 'dividing shrinks the number' and compute 4 ÷ 3 ≈ 1.3 instead of asking how many 1/3-foot pieces fit into 4 feet (each whole foot holds 3 thirds, so 4 × 3 = 12). Before you submit, check: if the divisor is a fraction smaller than 1, the quotient must be BIGGER than the dividend, not smaller.

level1.stem: A bag holds 6 cups of rice. One scoop is 1/2 cup. How many scoops of rice are in the bag?
level1.stemEs: Una bolsa tiene 6 tazas de arroz. Una cucharada grande es 1/2 taza. ¿Cuántas cucharadas grandes de arroz hay en la bolsa?
hints: Find how many 1/2-cup scoops fit in 6 cups. Find 6 ÷ 1/2.
hintsEs: Halla cuántas cucharadas de 1/2 taza caben en 6 tazas. Halla 6 ÷ 1/2.
level1.explanation: Write the division: 6 ÷ 1/2 Put a 1 under 6. Keep, Change, Flip: 6/1 × 2/1 = 12/1 = 12
level1.explanationEs: Escribe la división: 6 ÷ 1/2 Pon un 1 debajo del 6. Conserva, Cambia, Voltea: 6/1 × 2/1 = 12/1 = 12

hints: Write 3 as 3/1. Then keep, change, flip.
hintsEs: Escribe 3 como 3/1. Luego conserva, cambia, voltea.
level1.explanation: Put a 1 under the whole number: 3/1 ÷ 1/2 Keep, Change, Flip: 3/1 × 2/1 Multiply across: 3/1 × 2/1 = 6/1 = 6
level1.explanationEs: Pon un 1 debajo del número entero: 3/1 ÷ 1/2 Conserva, Cambia, Voltea: 3/1 × 2/1 Multiplica en línea recta: 3/1 × 2/1 = 6/1 = 6

hints: Write 2 as 2/1. Flip only the number you divide by.
hintsEs: Escribe 2 como 2/1. Voltea solo el número entre el que divides.
level1.explanation: Put a 1 under the whole number: 3/5 ÷ 2/1 Keep, Change, Flip: 3/5 × 1/2 Multiply across: 3/5 × 1/2 = 3/10
level1.explanationEs: Pon un 1 debajo del número entero: 3/5 ÷ 2/1 Conserva, Cambia, Voltea: 3/5 × 1/2 Multiplica en línea recta: 3/5 × 1/2 = 3/10

level2.stem: Leo says 1/2 ÷ 4 is 8. He flipped the 1/2 and multiplied: 2 × 4 = 8. Is he right? Find the correct answer.
level2.stemEs: Leo dice que 1/2 ÷ 4 es 8. Él volteó el 1/2 y multiplicó: 2 × 4 = 8. ¿Tiene razón? Halla la respuesta correcta.
hints: Keep the first number. Flip only the number you divide by. Write 4 as 4/1 first.
hintsEs: Conserva el primer número. Voltea solo el número entre el que divides. Primero escribe 4 como 4/1.
level2.explanation: Put a 1 under the whole number: 1/2 ÷ 4/1 Keep 1/2. Flip 4/1: 1/2 × 1/4 Multiply across: 1/2 × 1/4 = 1/8
level2.explanationEs: Pon un 1 debajo del número entero: 1/2 ÷ 4/1 Conserva 1/2. Voltea 4/1: 1/2 × 1/4 Multiplica en línea recta: 1/2 × 1/4 = 1/8

hints: Write 3 as 3/1. Keep, change, flip. Then simplify.
hintsEs: Escribe 3 como 3/1. Conserva, cambia, voltea. Luego simplifica.

level2.explanationEs: Conserva, Cambia, Voltea: 6/7 ÷ 3/1 → 6/7 × 1/3 Multiplica en línea recta. Simplifica: 6/7 × 1/3 = 6/21 = 2/7

hints: Put a 1 under the 4. Then keep, change, flip.
hintsEs: Pon un 1 debajo del 4. Luego conserva, cambia, voltea.
level2.explanation: Put a 1 under the whole number: 4/1 ÷ 1/5 Keep, Change, Flip: 4/1 × 5/1 Multiply across: 4/1 × 5/1 = 20/1 = 20

level2.stem: A fraction divided by 5 is 1/10. What is the fraction?
level2.stemEs: Una fracción dividida entre 5 es 1/10. ¿Cuál es la fracción?
hints: Dividing by 5 is the same as multiplying by 1/5. Work backward: multiply 1/10 by 5.
hintsEs: Dividir entre 5 es lo mismo que multiplicar por 1/5. Trabaja hacia atrás: multiplica 1/10 por 5.
level2.explanation: Undo the division. Multiply by 5: 1/10 × 5 = 5/10 = 1/2 Check with Keep, Change, Flip: 1/2 × 1/5 = 1/10
level2.explanationEs: Deshaz la división. Multiplica por 5: 1/10 × 5 = 5/10 = 1/2 Comprueba con Conserva, Cambia, Voltea: 1/2 × 1/5 = 1/10

level2.stem: A farmer has 5/6 acre of land. She splits it into 5 equal gardens. How big is each garden?
level2.stemEs: Una granjera tiene 5/6 de acre de tierra. La divide en 5 huertos iguales. ¿Qué tamaño tiene cada huerto?
hints: Find 5/6 ÷ 5. Write 5 as 5/1 first.
hintsEs: Halla 5/6 ÷ 5. Primero escribe 5 como 5/1.
level2.explanation: Put a 1 under the whole number: 5/6 ÷ 5/1 Keep, Change, Flip: 5/6 × 1/5 Multiply across. Simplify: 5/6 × 1/5 = 5/30 = 1/6
level2.explanationEs: Pon un 1 debajo del número entero: 5/6 ÷ 5/1 Conserva, Cambia, Voltea: 5/6 × 1/5 Multiplica en línea recta. Simplifica: 5/6 × 1/5 = 5/30 = 1/6

choiceFeedback: That is the reciprocal of the answer. Keep the 6 on top: 6/1 times 5/1.
That multiplies 6 by 1/5. Division flips the divisor first: 6/1 times 5/1.
That adds 6 and 5. Keep, change, flip, and then multiply.
level3.explanation: Put a 1 under the whole number so it becomes 6/1. Keep 6/1, change ÷ to ×, and flip 1/5 to its reciprocal 5/1. Multiply across: 6/1 × 5/1 = 30/1 = 30.

level3.stem: Nia says dividing always makes a number smaller. Find 7 ÷ 1/2 to test her idea.
level3.stemEs: Nia dice que dividir siempre hace más pequeño un número. Halla 7 ÷ 1/2 para probar su idea.
hints: Write 7 as 7/1. Keep, change, flip.
hintsEs: Escribe 7 como 7/1. Conserva, cambia, voltea.
level3.explanation: Keep, Change, Flip: 7/1 × 2/1 Multiply across: 7/1 × 2/1 = 14/1 = 14 Compare with 7: 14 > 7
level3.explanationEs: Conserva, Cambia, Voltea: 7/1 × 2/1 Multiplica en línea recta: 7/1 × 2/1 = 14/1 = 14 Compara con 7: 14 > 7

hints: Write 6 as 6/1. Keep, change, flip. Then simplify.

level3.stem: One lap of a track is 1/4 mile. Mo runs 9 miles. How many laps does he run?
level3.stemEs: Una vuelta a la pista es 1/4 de milla. Mo corre 9 millas. ¿Cuántas vueltas corre?
hints: How many 1/4-mile laps fit in 9 miles? Write the division first.
hintsEs: ¿Cuántas vueltas de 1/4 de milla caben en 9 millas? Primero escribe la división.
level3.explanation: Write the division: 9 ÷ 1/4 Keep, Change, Flip. Multiply: 9/1 × 4/1 = 36/1 = 36
level3.explanationEs: Escribe la división: 9 ÷ 1/4 Conserva, Cambia, Voltea. Multiplica: 9/1 × 4/1 = 36/1 = 36

level3.stem: A ribbon is 6 feet long. You cut it into 1/4-foot pieces. Then you cut each piece into 3 equal parts. How many small parts do you get?
level3.stemEs: Un listón mide 6 pies de largo. Lo cortas en piezas de 1/4 de pie. Luego cortas cada pieza en 3 partes iguales. ¿Cuántas partes pequeñas obtienes?
hints: First find the length of one small part: 1/4 ÷ 3. Then find how many fit in 6 feet.
hintsEs: Primero halla la longitud de una parte pequeña: 1/4 ÷ 3. Luego halla cuántas caben en 6 pies.
level3.explanation: Find the length of one small part: 1/4 ÷ 3 = 1/4 × 1/3 = 1/12 Find how many small parts fit: 6 ÷ 1/12 = 6/1 × 12/1 = 72
level3.explanationEs: Halla la longitud de una parte pequeña: 1/4 ÷ 3 = 1/4 × 1/3 = 1/12 Halla cuántas partes pequeñas caben: 6 ÷ 1/12 = 6/1 × 12/1 = 72
